title: China’s Human Rights Crisis Hasn’t Disappeared
gist: Benedict Rogers argues that at the Sept. 2026 Trump-Xi Washington summit Trump should press for release of named prisoners (Jimmy Lai, Joshua Wong, Zion Church pastors, John Cao, Min Zin, Uyghur and Tibetan detainees) and tie better US-China relations to religious freedom and an end to transnational repression. He also urges explicit deterrence on Taiwan, saying Trump's Greenland and Canada claims have emboldened Beijing.

insights.claim: Xi Jinping's Sept. 2026 meeting with Trump in Washington carries an agenda spanning tariffs, trade, AI and Taiwan, following a prior leaders' meeting in Beijing in May.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Summit cadence (Beijing in May, Washington in September) points to an active US-China bargaining track on tariffs and tech.
insights.quote: there will be many issues on their agenda, from tariffs and trade to artificial intelligence and Taiwan.
insights.locator: When Chinese President Xi Jinping meets

insights.claim: Trump showed he can extract prisoner releases: after he pressed Xi in Beijing in May, China freed Zion Church founder Ezra Jin Mingri less than two months later and let him leave for the US.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Beijing is willing to trade humanitarian gestures for summit goodwill, a sign of transactional rather than frozen relations.
insights.quote: Trump has shown that he can secure the release of prisoners when he chooses to.
insights.locator: When the two leaders met in Beijing

insights.claim: Rogers argues Trump should make clear that US-China relations cannot improve while the CCP persecutes religious believers, framing Xi's Sinicization of religion and laws like Hong Kong's national security law and the new ethnic unity law as roadblocks.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: If adopted, human-rights linkage would add a non-economic constraint on any US-China trade thaw.

insights.claim: China's new ethnic unity law criminalizes criticism of the CCP wherever it takes place around the world, an extraterritorial reach.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Extraterritorial speech laws raise legal and reputational risk for firms, academics and employees with China exposure.
insights.quote: the new ethnic unity law, which criminalizes criticism of the CCP wherever it takes place around the world.

insights.claim: The State Department on Sept. 10, 2026 again recognized the treatment of Uyghurs as genocide, a designation made by both Trump administrations and the Biden administration.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Bipartisan genocide designation sustains supply-chain compliance risk (Xinjiang sourcing) regardless of trade détente.

insights.claim: Jimmy Lai, 78, is serving a 20-year sentence after six years already in jail, and Rogers warns he will die in prison without sustained international pressure; his daughter's cancer diagnosis strengthens the humanitarian case.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Lai's case is a bellwether for Hong Kong rule-of-law perceptions among international businesses.
insights.quote: Lai, who has already spent the past six years in jail, will die in prison if international pressure for his release is not sustained.
insights.locator: Trump must also prioritize Hong Kong

insights.claim: Joshua Wong, now 29, faces new 'collusion with foreign forces' charges under Hong Kong's national security law that could bring a life sentence; Rogers says the US bears special responsibility after refusing him asylum in 2020.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Escalating national-security prosecutions keep Hong Kong's political risk premium elevated.
insights.locator: There are other Hong Kong prisoner cases

insights.claim: US citizen and Myanmar-born scholar Min Zin was arrested at the airport in China in June after being invited to an academic conference in Kunming and remains detained.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Detention of invited foreign academics raises personnel travel risk for anyone visiting China.
insights.locator: The case of U.S. citizen Min Zin

insights.claim: China pressured the U.S.-China Catholic Association into withdrawing a keynote invitation to Chinese professor Yang Fenggang, which Rogers cites alongside secret Chinese police stations in the US and UK as transnational repression.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Chinese influence operations inside US institutions are a durable irritant that could trigger new countermeasures.
insights.locator: The CCP’s campaign of transnational repression

insights.claim: Rogers contends Trump's own claims to Greenland and Canada have emboldened China's stance toward Taiwan, and only Xi's conviction that the US will defend Taiwan will deter an invasion or blockade.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: US territorial rhetoric may erode deterrence norms and raise Taiwan Strait tail risk.
insights.quote: Trump’s own claims of U.S. ownership of Greenland and Canada have served to embolden China’s stance toward Taiwan.

insights.claim: Rogers argues Trump should state that US arms supplies to Taiwan will continue and that any act of war, including an economic blockade, would carry severe consequences.
insights.speaker: Benedict Rogers
insights.so_what: Explicit blockade language would matter for shipping and semiconductor supply-chain risk pricing.
